newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Business as usual on key NZ economic areas - Manfed.
newsitem.headline: Business as usual on key NZ economic areas - Manfed.

text.p: Manufacturers on Tuesday night welcomed the form of the new government saying it looked like "business as usual" on key economic areas.
"From what we heard, it looks like business as usual on the major economic parameters," Manufacturers Federation chief executive Simon Arnold told NZPA.

"I don't see much change in terms of the kind of discussions over the Reserve Bank and there is not a lot of change under the Employment Contracts Act, and no change under the fiscal responsibility act, so that is all good news."
Judging any changes to social policy would have to wait until details were available tomorrow, Arnold said.

"Exporters will be looking towards Winston Peters, as the new treasurer, to show fiscal restraint in the short-term...High spending would further push up the dollar and reduce investment in new jobs," he said.

"We obviously welcome any new government and would look forward to working constructively with it over the period ahead with the objective of continuing to build on economic growth and also to improve the social conditions within New Zealand.

"In that regard, I suppose we are looking particularly at the return to work area and helping those New Zealanders who are out of work to get back into the workforce and seeing social investment in that area and the area of building a better education system in terms of lifting the skill level of New Zealanders," Arnold added.

Michael Barnett, chief executive of Auckland Regional Chamber of Commerce and Industry said: "Ignore the political parties and politicians and look closely at the policies the new government offers to the country along with the compromises they have made in order to secure them the right to the treasury

In welcoming the new government, Barnett added in a statement that business and business organisations -- which have themselves been reformed over the last ten year -- should also be careful in their response to the new government.
"The arrival of our first coalition government in modern times reinforces the point that government too is moving through a transformation that it may not get it right in its first attempt," he said.

Earlier on Tuesday the nationalist NZ First Party chose the caretaker National Party government as its preferred coalition partner after almost two months of negotiations with both National and Labour.
